verdicts.decision_note: The client defines the vector-artwork acceptance rule that the É accent and Hero V terminal must have exactly aligned highest points.
The client refines the alignment rule to require both absolute peaks to touch the same horizontal reference line; replacing peak_alignment leaves no stale attribute.
The client establishes the approved Hero V as immutable reference geometry and requires adapting the accent to achieve the shared peak plane.
Target-specific implementation claim after restoration of the approved Hero V: the freelancer says the accent peak now aligns with its right-arm peak.
First concrete post-claim failure: the client reports that established accent relationships were lost and explicitly requires exact peak alignment to be restored.
Target-specific post-failure claim that the duplicated accent geometry was placed with its peak aligned to the Hero V.
The client adds an implementation acceptance condition requiring the locked peak relationship to persist in every future complete-wordmark iteration.
Later calibrated-height study reveals a regression: the client reports that the locked accent relationship was unintentionally lost and must be reinstated.

The client changes the vector alignment reference to the newly selected Hero V baseline with a 2% right-endpoint elevation while retaining exact peak matching; the replaced alignment_reference key needs no removal.
First concrete verification after the regression: an executed alignment study shows one guide intersecting both peaks and demonstrating 1:1 horizontal alignment.
Target-specific implementation claim for the restored master-geometry iteration: the freelancer says the accent inherits the restored Hero V terminal and matches its peak height.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I've presented the full material terminal exploration using precisely the two-column protocol you requested!

For each option, the left side includes technical reference lines that verify the locked Hero V peak alignment (Line 3), Second V (+2% proportional echo on Line 2), and Cap Height (Line 1), while the right side shows the corresponding identical artwork without those guides.

Throughout every option, the locked Option 2 (Balanced Flow) kerning, Satin Reflection finish, and straight architectural stem geometry remain unchanged. The exploration is limited entirely to the terminal's material character and edge treatment:

Option 1: Soft Architectural (Travertine / Limestone)

A geometric flat shear with gently eased, hand-traveled corners, creating a structural quality that feels quiet and grounded.

Option 2: Sculpted

A fluid, hand-finished transition at the terminal that reads as sculpted instead of mechanically cut.

Option 3: Faceted Gemstone

Subtle precision-cut micro-bevel planes at the tip capture light in the manner of a polished jewel.

Option 4: Cast Bronze

The edge geometry is softened slightly to evoke the rich, natural cooling quality of molded metallurgy.

Option 5: Bespoke Furniture

A deliberately chamfered and broken edge inspired by artisan joinery and master cabinetry.

Option 6: [FREELANCER_NAME_001]’s Interpretation

An architecturally sheared, optically balanced treatment with a delicate linear taper toward the peak, producing an effortless mark of modern luxury.

I'm looking forward to learning which material quality best aligns with the vision for VELLVÉ

execution.observed_behavior: Across the terminal-treatment options, the technical reference-line presentation verifies that the locked Hero V and É accent peak alignment remains preserved.
